cap: Pulsatile GnRH releases LH, which drives Leydig cells to make testosterone, and FSH, which drives Sertoli cells to make androgen-binding protein and inhibin B. Testosterone and estradiol brake GnRH and LH, while inhibin B brakes only FSH. Testosterone then acts directly, becomes DHT through 5-alpha-reductase, or becomes estradiol through aromatization in fat, and each form has its own targets.
teach: Use the feedback panel to read lab patterns. Germ cell loss lowers inhibin B, so FSH rises alone. Leydig cell failure lowers testosterone, so LH and FSH both rise. Exogenous testosterone suppresses LH and FSH, so the testis shrinks and sperm production stops even though serum testosterone is high.
